cards.explanation: The answer is to keep walking in Him, friends. The letter says, "…just as you have received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to walk in Him…" (Colossians 2:6). Walking is one step after another, day after day. It's like stamping a batch of cookies, one at a time, until the tray is full.

The answer is True. The letter says, "…established in the faith as you were taught…" (Colossians 2:7). Everyone is to stay planted in the faith they were taught, friends. No need to go hunting for a brand new recipe.

The answer is Christ. The letter says this philosophy and empty deception is based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world "…rather than on Christ." (Colossians 2:8). So the contrast here is with Christ, friends. Empty deception, like a pretty box with no cookies inside.

The answer is bodily, and that's the word the letter uses. "For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form." (Colossians 2:9). All the fullness, friends, not a sample or a taste. That's why nothing clever needs to be added on top of Him.
The answer is False. The letter says, "…you have been made complete in Christ…" (Colossians 2:10). Nothing is left over that anyone needs to go find somewhere else, friends. In Him, the job is done.

The answer is every ruler and authority. The letter says Christ "…is the head over every ruler and authority." (Colossians 2:10). Every one, friends, with nobody left out. That's a big title, and it's why we can stand firm.

The answer is their sinful nature. The letter says, "In Him you were also circumcised, in the putting off of your sinful nature…" (Colossians 2:11). Something heavy gets taken off, friends. I know that feeling, like finally taking off an apron after a very long bake.

The answer is hands. It was "…the circumcision performed by Christ and not by human hands." (Colossians 2:11). The contrast is between Christ and human hands, friends. Christ is the one who performed it.

The answer is that they were raised with Him! "And having been buried with Him in baptism, you were raised with Him…" (Colossians 2:12). Buried is not the end of that sentence, friends. The letter says they were raised through faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead. That's the part that gets me excited.

The answer is through faith in God's power. They were raised "…through your faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead." (Colossians 2:12). The power belongs to God, friends, and faith is how they trust it. It's the same power that raised Christ.

The answer is that God made them alive with Christ. "When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ." (Colossians 2:13). Dead to alive, friends. Notice who does the work: God. That's about as big a turnaround as there is.
The answer is all. "He forgave us all our trespasses…" (Colossians 2:13). All, friends, with nothing held back or kept on a shelf for later. That's a lot of grace.

The answer is True. The letter says He was "…having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us." (Colossians 2:14). Canceled means it's no longer owed, friends. The bill is gone.

The answer is the cross. The letter says, "He took it away, nailing it to the cross!" (Colossians 2:14). That debt isn't just set aside, friends, it's taken away. The cross is where the verse says it went.

The answer is that they were disarmed. The letter says, "…having disarmed the powers and authorities…" (Colossians 2:15). God is the one who did the disarming, friends. Picture the scary guy showing up with nothing but an empty oven mitt.

The answer is False. The letter says God "…made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross." (Colossians 2:15). The verse says a public spectacle, friends, not somewhere nobody could see. The triumph came by the cross.
